hero.sub: An alarm going off in the garden unit, a basement toilet that won't flush or a sewer smell near the basin. We repair and replace ejector pumps in Lincoln Park homes and buildings. Our office is on Diversey Parkway. Open 24/7.

blocks.body: Fixtures below the sewer line, like a garden unit bathroom or a basement laundry, drain into a sealed basin. The ejector pump lifts that wastewater up into the building's main line. A float starts the pump, and a check valve keeps water from flowing back. If any part fails, the basin fills and the fixtures back up.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber working on the discharge pipe of a basement sump pump

blocks.h2: Signs Your Ejector Pump Is Failing

tiles.body: A worn seal or vent problem.

tiles.h3: The Pump Runs All the Time
tiles.body: A stuck float or bad check valve.

blocks.intro: Garden units and finished basements are common here, and many depend on an ejector pump.

items.body: Grease and wipes are hard on pumps. Good habits help them last.
In a converted basement, the pump handles every basement drain.
In a condo building, the pump may be a common element. We document what we find.
We test the alarm every visit.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton
blocks.intro: We fix the pump and explain why it failed.

steps.body: Pump, float, valve, seal and vent.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber in shoe covers on a home's front steps with a sewer camera

blocks.h2: Ejector Pumps in Finished Garden Units
blocks.body: In finished garden units, the ejector basin is often hidden under a floor panel or in a closet. That's fine, as long as it can be reached for service. When we replace a pump, we check that the lid seals tightly, the vent is clear and the alarm can be heard from the living space. If the basin is buried under flooring, we'll talk about adding an access panel.

blocks.h2: Ejector Pump Questions From Lincoln Park Homeowners

items.q: The alarm is on in the garden unit. What should we do?
items.preview: Stop using the basement fixtures and call us.
items.answer: Stop using every fixture that drains to the basin, including the garden unit's sinks, toilet and laundry, and call us.

items.q: How long do ejector pumps last?
items.answer: Often around 7 to 10 years, depending on use.

items.q: Why does it smell like sewage downstairs?
items.preview: A worn seal, vent or dry trap.
items.answer: Usually a worn lid seal, a vent issue or a dry floor drain trap.

items.q: Can you add a backup pump?
items.answer: Some basins can hold two pumps. We'll check yours.

items.q: Can a basin be moved during a remodel?
items.answer: Sometimes. It's easiest to plan before the floor goes in.

items.q: How much does ejector pump replacement cost in Lincoln Park?
items.preview: It depends on the pump and basin. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the pump, the basin and access. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
